subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw's web egress boundary be a scoped web_fetch hostname allowlist, an operator-managed proxy boundary, or a cross-tool fetch/search/browser allow-and-deny policy?
rationale: This creates an operator-trusted security/config surface, and the currently related PRs encode different boundary choices that automation should not pick without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist First
options.body: Review and sponsor the focused hostname-allowlist path for web_fetch as an incremental first step, while leaving deny/search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Make Managed Proxy The Boundary
options.body: Pause local web_fetch config work and make application-owned egress policy belong to the managed proxy direction instead.

options.title: Require Cross-Tool Design
options.body: Hold implementation until a broader design covers fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, proxy routing, and deny semantics together.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped web_fetch Allowlist First
recommendation.body: Review and sponsor the focused hostname-allowlist path for web_fetch as an incremental first step, while leaving deny/search/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest combined recent history across SSRF, guarded fetch, web_fetch runtime, and config surfaces involved in the boundary choice.
